summary.title: Some blogging myths
summary.one_liner: Eight common myths that discourage people from blogging (you don't need to be original, an expert, or 100% correct) and why writing for one reader and publishing short posts helps.
keywords: do i need to be an expert to blog
takeaways: Write about things you found confusing; others probably did too, even if information exists online.
You only need to know a couple of things the reader doesn't; experts are not required.
Use qualifiers like 'I think' for uncertain statements instead of fact-checking everything.
Write for one specific person (a friend, coworker, or past self) to keep posts clear.
Publish short posts rather than waiting to include everything; blogging is not for everyone.
summary.summary: Julia Evans expands a talk on myths that stop people from blogging, listing eight myths: needing to be original, an expert, 100% correct, interesting, to explain every concept, page views mattering, more material being better, and everyone should blog. Each myth gets a short section with personal examples, such as hedging statements with "I think", choosing one reader to write for, and ignoring page view analytics in favor of comments. The post also covers how she handles pedantic comments by reading them all, not replying, and sometimes updating posts. It is a personal essay rather than a how-to, so it offers opinions and experience rather than technical instructions.
